hălōs , ō, f., = ἅλως (a round threshing-floor),
I.a circle round the sun or moon, a halo, pure Lat. corona: “circa solem visum coloris varii circulum, qualis esse in arcu solet. Hunc Graeci halo vocant: nos dicere coronam aptissime possumus, etc.,” Sen. Q. N. 1, 2, 1 .—Called also hălysis (prob. corrupted from ἅλως), App. de Mundo, p. 64, 16.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
